audit_findings.title: One injury row has a blank Team cell on the official PDF — and the canonical dataset is right to leave it blank
audit_findings.detail: Row 18 of the 04:30 AM ET report prints 'Traore, Nolan, Probable, Injury/Illness - Right Calf Tightness / Soreness' with the Game Date, Game Time, Matchup and Team cells empty, because it is the first row of the PDF's second table. This audit's first transcription filled the Team cell in as BKN from the block heading above it. The canonical artefact leaves the cell empty. Leaving it empty is the correct behaviour under the project's no-inference rule, so the audit capture was corrected to blank and the value is published as blank. Consequence for readers: the player's team is not established by this row alone.

irregularities: The official page prints the same matchup twice inside this window: NYK@TOR on 2026-11-15 (game 0022600241) and again on 2026-11-17 (game 0022600253), both at Scotiabank Arena; and POR@MIN on 2026-11-16 (0022600250) and again on 2026-11-17 (0022600254), both at Target Center. This is what the official page says. It is flagged for manual review rather than corrected.

Game IDs 0022600256 (CHA@LAL, 11:00 PM ET) and 0022600257 (UTA@LAC, 10:30 PM ET) are out of chronological order on the page: 0022600256 is printed after 0022600257. The IDs are used as keys, so the ordering is published as printed.
Chunk 2 of 9 ends in the middle of 2026-11-18; no 11/18 game is part of this window and none was transcribed.
The canonical injury artefact is the 04:15 AM ET report; the newest report on the official index at read time was the 04:30 AM ET report. The comparison above is what establishes whether they agree.

One canonical injury row carries cell_provenance 'page-break gap' and six carry 'block-heading': the PDF drops repeated date/time/matchup cells, so those cells were reconstructed by the capturing session rather than read directly off the page. The row-by-row comparison here uses the reconstructed values, so it cannot independently prove the reconstruction; it can only show that the two reports agree.
